data.narrative:
Arbor Energy is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Brad Hartwig that has raised $96M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine frontier-tech peers in Climate & Energy: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using $96M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, this method implies a valuation of $192M. A peer-median approach could not be deployed: while eight same-sector comparables exist, none yielded sufficient datapoints (≥3) when filtered for identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier, making sector-wide aggregation unreliable and methodologically unsound.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $163M to $221M, with a median point estimate of $192M. This estimate rests entirely on stage-progression mechanics applied to deployed capital. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrowly comparable recent financings in the subsector—a constraint that limits triangulation robustness—and the sensitivity of the 2.0x multiplier to market conditions and capital availability. Any valuation discussion should acknowledge this single-method foundation and the early-stage risk profile typical of frontier-energy ventures.
